title: Noise-aware fidelity harness for FP8/INT8 transition
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a reproducible, noise-aware evaluation harness and scorer library to validate accuracy and fidelity when migrating model serving profiles from FP16 to FP8/INT8. The focus is on per-task and per-profile acceptance gating, robust aggregation across heterogeneous tasks, and instrumentation for drift detection during calibration workflows.
background: We have many ad-hoc quant validation pipelines that measure task accuracy and perplexity against FP16. However, as we introduce FP8 and INT8 profiles we need a standardized, conservative method to surface regressions that accounts for quantization-induced stochasticity and task heterogeneity. Existing artifacts (various ENG tickets) are fragmented; this ticket consolidates an approach and delivers a reusable scorer harness and dashboard hooks.
goals: Implement a noise-aware fidelity metric that combines perplexity, task accuracy (MMLU-style), and lexical overlap metrics (ROUGE/BLEU) into a single composite score
Provide a reference-less instruction-adherence scorer for structured outputs (JSON schema matching + token-level F1)
Add stochastic quantization noise experiments and signal aggregation to estimate uncertainty and confidence intervals for metric deltas
Integrate scorer library with eval-runner and Redwood metrics pipeline; expose per-profile gating decisions in Console
Define numeric acceptance criteria and automated gating for rollout (canary/fallback)
approach: Scorer library: implement modular scorers (perplexity, accuracy, BLEU, ROUGE-L, BERTScore-lite, instruction-adherence) with a common interface
Normalization: per-task z-score normalization against FP16 baseline distributions with robust estimators (median and MAD) to avoid outlier sensitivity
Aggregation: harmonic-weighted aggregator that reduces dominance of high-token-count tasks and emphasizes relative drops for low-support tasks
Uncertainty: run N=30 stochastic quant seeds by applying simulated quant noise (per-layer scale jitter) and report mean + 95% CI for each metric
Reference-less fidelity: compute structural schema match ratio and constrained token-F1 to handle tasks without a single golden reference
Gating: composite_score = weighted sum(harmonic_agg(normalized_metrics)) with weight tuning by task criticality; gate fails if composite drop from FP16 > 2% with CI not overlapping 0
Telemetry: emit metric deltas, CI, per-layer activation deviation histogram to Console; flag anomalies via existing alerting rules
acceptance_criteria: Scorer library merged to repo: redwood/inference/eval/scorers (PR #1294)
CI runs produce stable mean+CI for each metric across N=30 stochastic seeds
Per-task absolute accuracy drop <= 1.5% (for classification tasks) compared to FP16 baseline or within CI overlap
BLEU drop <= 2.0 points and ROUGE-L drop <= 1.5 points for translation/summarization tasks
Perplexity increase <= 5% relative to FP16 baseline
Composite score drop <= 2% with 95% CI including 0 for promoted profiles
Console dashboard panel shows per-profile metric deltas and gate decision for at least 5 production profiles
Documentation and runbook published in Confluence: /display/INF/Noise-aware+Fidelity+Harness
implementation_notes: Prefer pure Python scorer implementations compatible with our eval-runner; keep heavy ops optional (BERTScore-lite uses sentence-transformer embeddings cached per-task)
Use reservoir sampling for large prompt corpora to keep run-time bounded during N=30 stochastic runs
Store raw per-seed outputs in ephemeral bucket with retention 14 days; aggregated metrics stored in metrics-store with 1y retention
Ensure scorers are deterministic given seed; expose seed in eval metadata
Add configuration knobs: seeds, per-task weight, normalization method (z/mad/minmax), aggregator type
Make the harness callable from both offline evals and on-hosting canaries for rollback decisions

decisions: Use harmonic-weighted aggregation instead of plain mean to avoid high-token tasks dominating the composite score
Normalize metrics per-task using z-score with MAD fallback to handle skewed distributions
Run N=30 stochastic seeds as default for CI-level validation; use N=100 for final pre-production promotion when compute budget allows
Treat BLEU/ROUGE as secondary signals and cap their weight to avoid overshadowing semantic fidelity metrics
